methodologyNotes: Covers external canister filters and hang-on-back (HOB) power filters for freshwater aquariums that a buyer comparison-shops in 2026, spanning budget (SunSun) to premium (Fluval FX6, OASE BioMaster Thermo) tiers. type is an enum: canister (fully sealed external unit, gravity/siphon fed) or hang-on-back (HOB; clips onto the tank rim, impeller-driven intake tube). tank_size_gal is the manufacturer's maximum rated aquarium size in US gallons; when the manufacturer publishes a min-max range, this is the top of that range. flow_rate_gph is the manufacturer's rated pump output in US gallons per hour — the raw pump figure, not a derated "in-tank filter circulation" number, when a source publishes both. media_capacity_l is the media basket/tray/canister filter-volume in liters as explicitly stated by the manufacturer; null when no liter figure is disclosed (common for HOB filters, which are usually specified by included cartridge/insert count instead). media_stages counts the manufacturer's own explicitly stated filtration-stage number (e.g. "4 STAGE FILTRATION" printed on AquaClear/Magniflow packaging, "5-stage" for the SunSun HW-304B) or, when no explicit stage count is published but the manufacturer names discrete filtration categories (mechanical/chemical/biological), the count of those named categories; null when neither is stated. wattage is the filter pump's rated power draw in watts at the 120V/60Hz US spec (or the single spec given, where regional variants exist); for the OASE BioMaster Thermo 850 — the one model here with a built-in heater — this is the pump only, the separate 400W heater element is called out in the product's provenance/priceNote instead of blended into wattage. self_priming is true only where the manufacturer explicitly describes an automatic/self-starting pump that needs no manual siphon step (e.g. Fluval's "Smart Pump" auto-start, a stated "self-priming pump", or a push-button primer described as self-priming); it is false where the manufacturer instead describes a manual hand-operated primer bulb/handle (Fluval's 07-series "Redesigned Primer" requires the user to hand-pump it); null where the manufacturer's page does not address priming at all. dimensions_in is length x width x height in inches as published, converted from mm/cm where the manufacturer only gives metric; cylindrical canisters are given as diameter x diameter x height. priceUsd is a representative current US street price (a named US retailer or the manufacturer's own USD listing) since most of these manufacturers' own product pages do not publish MSRP; null when no verbatim US-dollar figure could be sourced from a fetched page — several long-running EU-market products (OASE, both EHEIM Classic sizes) and two Fluval 07-series filters had no fetchable USD price and are left null rather than guessed. releaseDate is left null across the board: none of the fetched manufacturer or retailer pages stated a verbatim launch year/month for these long-running, frequently-restocked product lines, and none was fabricated.

products.name: Fluval FX6 Canister Filter
products.priceNote: Aquariums Direct USA (aquariumsdirectusa.com) lists the FX6 at $369.99 (shown as out of stock at the time fetched); no MSRP is published on Fluval's own product page. Aquarium Source's independent review cites a different retailer at $404.39, so street price visibly fluctuates; the lower, more MSRP-like figure was used.
products.provenance: Fluval's official US product page states verbatim: pump output "925 US GPH / 3500 LPH", filter circulation "563 US GPH / 2130 LPH", tank size "up to 400 US gallons (1,500 L)", media basket volume "1.5 gallons (5.9 L)", power "43W (120V/60Hz)", dimensions "15.75in L x 15.75in W x 20.8in H", and self-starting Smart Pump operation ("just add water, plug in and Smart Pump will take over") — used here for type, flow_rate_gph (pump output), tank_size_gal, media_capacity_l, media_stages (mechanical/chemical/biological named as the multi-stage system), wattage, self_priming, and dimensions_in. Aquarium Source's review independently corroborates the 925/563 GPH split, "up to 400 gallons", "15 x 15 x 20 inches", and "5.9 liters" media capacity, while noting the manufacturer's advertised 925 GPH is optimistic versus real-world 563 GPH — both figures are Fluval's own, so 925 (pump output) was kept for consistency with how flow_rate_gph is defined across this dataset. No verbatim USD MSRP appears on Fluval's page; priceUsd/priceNote draw on two retailers instead.

products.name: Fluval FX4 Canister Filter
products.priceNote: Aquarium Source's dedicated FX4 review cites $333.04 at the retailer it checked; a separate Aquarium Source "best canister filter" roundup cites $331.99 at another retailer around the same time. Fluval's own product page does not publish a price.
products.provenance: Fluval's official US product page states verbatim: pump output "700 US GPH / 2650 LPH", filter circulation "450 US GPH / 1700 LPH", tank size "up to 250 US gallons (1000 L)", media basket capacity "1 gallon (3.9 L)", multi-stage mechanical/chemical/biological media, power "30W (120V/60Hz)", Smart Pump self-starting operation, and dimensions "15.75in L x 15.75in W x 16.5in H" — used directly for every spec field. Aquamarine Power's independent review corroborates 700 GPH, "up to 250 gallons", "30 watts", "1 gallon (3.9 liters)" media capacity, self-priming ("Yes (automatic)"), and "4 removable baskets", plus measured 28dB noise and a $350-400 street-price range not used here since the two Aquarium Source figures are more specific. No verbatim USD MSRP appears on Fluval's own page.

products.name: Fluval 407 Performance Canister Filter
products.priceNote: No verbatim USD price could be sourced from a fetched page: Fluval's own product page does not list one, Chewy/PetSmart/Amazon pages returned bot-verification or 429/503 responses when fetched, and no aquarium-review site with a dedicated 407 write-up and price could be reached (aquariumsource.com's 407 review page 404's).
products.provenance: Fluval's official US product page states verbatim: pump output "383 US GPH / 1450 LPH", filter circulation "245 US GPH / 930 LPH" (flow_rate_gph uses the pump-output figure for consistency with the FX-series entries), recommended tank size "50-100 US Gal / 150-500 L" (top of range used), media basket capacity "4.2 L", power "23W (120V/60Hz)" / "20W (230-240V/50Hz)", and dimensions "9.5in L x 7in W x 19.3in H". The page explicitly describes a "Redesigned Primer with larger easy-grip handle" — a hand-operated primer, not an automatic self-starting pump like the FX-series' Smart Pump — so self_priming is false. The page names specific media components (Bio-Foam Max, Bio-Foam, Carbon, a vertical pre-filter cartridge) but never labels them with a stage count or the mechanical/chemical/biological framing used elsewhere on Fluval's own site, so media_stages is left null rather than guessed at 3-5.

products.name: Fluval 307 Performance Canister Filter
products.priceNote: Aquarium Source's canister-filter roundup shows the 307 on sale for $179.82 "on sale from $199.99" at the retailer it checked; $199.99 (the stated list price) is used as priceUsd. Fluval's own product page does not publish a price.
products.provenance: Fluval's official US product page states verbatim: pump output "303 US GPH / 1150 LPH", filter circulation "206 US GPH / 780 LPH" (pump-output figure used for flow_rate_gph), tank size "40-70 US gallons (90-330 L)" (top of range used), basket volume "3.1 L" (of a 4.5 L total chamber / 7.3 L canister volume), power "16W (120V/60Hz)" / "15W (230-240V/50Hz)", dimensions "9.5in L x 7in W x 16.5in H", and the same hand-operated "Redesigned Primer" described for the 407 (not an automatic self-starting pump), so self_priming is false. Aquarium Source's roundup independently corroborates "303 US gal/h", "40-70 gallons", and the sale/list pricing. No explicit stage count or mechanical/chemical/biological labeling appears on the manufacturer page, so media_stages is null.

products.name: EHEIM Classic 2217 (600) External Canister Filter
products.priceNote: No verbatim USD price could be sourced from a fetched page — several US retailer product pages (AquaCave, That Fish Place, Amazon) returned 404s or blocked content when fetched. This is a long-running EU-manufactured product line typically sold in the US through smaller specialty importers.
products.provenance: EHEIM's official parts/product page for the classic 600 (article 2217010) states verbatim: pump output "ca. 1000 l" per hour at 50Hz (≈264 US gal/h, the figure independently used by several US retailer listings for the same model, so it was kept as flow_rate_gph), "für Aquarien bis ca. 600l" (≈160 US gal max, rounding matches how US listings describe this model), "Filtervolumen: 6l" media volume, "Leistungsaufnahme (50Hz): 20 Watt", and dimensions "Höhe 400mm, Durchmesser Ø 205mm" (converted to 15.75in height x 8.1in diameter; given as diameter x diameter x height since the canister is cylindrical). The page does not state a specific filtration-stage count (it only describes compatibility with "filter pads and loose filter media"), and does not address whether the pump is self-priming (EHEIM Classic filters are widely known in the hobby to require a manual siphon-start rather than an integrated primer, but since no fetched EHEIM page states this explicitly, self_priming is left null rather than assumed).

products.name: EHEIM Classic 2213 (250) External Canister Filter
products.priceNote: No verbatim USD price could be sourced from a fetched page for the same reasons as the 2217: US retailer product pages returned 404s or blocked content when fetched.
products.provenance: EHEIM's official parts/product page for the classic 250 (article 2213010) states verbatim: pump output "ca. 440 l" per hour at 50Hz, "für Aquarien bis ca. 250l", "Filtervolumen: 3l", "Leistungsaufnahme (50Hz): 8 Watt", and dimensions "Höhe 355mm, Durchmesser Ø 160mm" (converted to 14.0in height x 6.3in diameter). US retailer listings for this exact model independently describe it as "110GPH" for "20-62 Gallons" (up to 66 gallons at some retailers) with "Power Consumption: 8W" and "Filter Volume: 3.0 Liters", matching the EHEIM-stated wattage and media volume and used here for flow_rate_gph (the commonly-cited US-market GPH figure) and tank_size_gal. No stage count or self-priming statement appears on the fetched manufacturer page, so both are null.

products.name: AquaClear 110 Power Filter
products.priceNote: Aquatic Warehouse (aquaticwarehouse.com) lists the AC110 at $99.99. Fluval's own AquaClear product page (Hagen/Fluval manufactures AquaClear) does not publish a price.
products.provenance: Fluval's official AquaClear product page states verbatim, for item 19620 (AC110): "500 US GPH / 1892 LPH" maximum flow, "60-110 US Gal / 227-416 L" tank capacity (top of range used), dimensions "13.6in L x 6.9in W x 9.2in H", power "14W" (same at 120V/60Hz and 230-240V/50Hz), and included media of 1 intake sponge, 2 carbon inserts, and 2 BIOMAX cartridges. The retail packaging (used as the image) explicitly prints "SUPERIOR 4 STAGE FILTRATION", "FOR AQUARIUMS 60-110 US Gal", and "PUMP OUTPUT 500 US GPH", confirming both media_stages=4 and the flow/tank figures. Aquatic Warehouse's listing independently corroborates "500 GPH", "60 to 100 gallon", the dimensions, and supplies the $99.99 US price absent from Fluval's own page. No fetched page states whether the AC110's pump is self-priming (Fluval's materials don't use that term for AquaClear, unlike its Tidal-competitor language for other brands), so self_priming and media_capacity_l (no basket volume in liters is given, only insert counts) are left null.

products.name: AquaClear 70 Power Filter
products.priceNote: Aquatic Warehouse (aquaticwarehouse.com) lists the AC70 at $79.99. Fluval's own AquaClear product page does not publish a price.
products.provenance: Fluval's official AquaClear product page states verbatim, for item 19615 (AC70): "300 US GPH / 1136 LPH" maximum flow, "40-70 US Gal / 152-265 L" tank capacity (top of range used), dimensions "8.5in L x 6.1in W x 8.6in H", power "7W (120V/60Hz)" / "5W (230-240V/50Hz)", and included media of one Bio-Foam, one Carbon, one BIOMAX, and one Intake Sponge insert. The retail packaging (used as the image) prints "SUPERIOR 4 STAGE FILTRATION", "FOR AQUARIUMS 40-70 US Gal", and "PUMP OUTPUT 300 US GPH", confirming media_stages=4 and the flow/tank figures. Aquatic Warehouse's listing independently confirms the $79.99 US price. media_capacity_l and self_priming are null for the same reasons given for the AC110 (no liter figure or priming statement on any fetched page).

products.name: Penn-Plax Cascade 1000 Canister Filter
products.priceNote: No verbatim USD price could be sourced from a fetched page: Penn-Plax's own storefront (eorder.pennplax.com) requires a trade login to view pricing, and Chewy/Walmart/Amazon pages returned bot-verification or rate-limit responses when fetched.
products.provenance: Penn-Plax's own product listing (and matching retail packaging shown in the product image, which prints "AQUARIUMS UP TO 100 GALLONS / 380 LITERS" and "PUMPS / POMPES 265 GPH / 1000 LPH") states: flow rate "265 gallons per hour", suitable "for aquariums up to 100 gallons", power "28.5 watts at 110 volts, 60Hz", dimensions "11.5in (width) x 10in (depth) x 17in (height)", a "push-button primer" described as self-priming, and three media types (poly fiber floss, bio-sponge, activated carbon) across "three large capacity media baskets" supporting physical/biological/chemical filtration — used for media_stages=3. No basket volume in liters is given, so media_capacity_l is null, and no USD price is available from any fetched page.

products.name: Marineland Magniflow 360 Canister Filter
products.priceNote: No verbatim USD price could be sourced from a fetched page: Marineland's own product page does not list one, and retailer pages checked (CountryMax, Petco, Big Al's) returned 404s or blocked content when fetched.
products.provenance: Marineland's official product page describes the Magniflow line as "multi-stage filtration" via "Stack N' Flo Filter Trays" providing "mechanical, chemical, and biological filtration", with a "Quick Prime Button" that "Fills filter chamber with water for self-priming system startup" (self_priming=true). The retail packaging (used as the image) explicitly prints "MAGNIFLOW 360 CANISTER FILTER", "Powerful, Complete 3 Stage Filtration for Fresh and Saltwater Aquariums", "FILTERS 360 gallons per hour", and "FOR UP TO 100 gallon aquarium", confirming flow_rate_gph, tank_size_gal, and media_stages=3. No fetched page (manufacturer or retailer) discloses a wattage figure, media basket volume in liters, or physical dimensions in inches for this model, so those three fields are null rather than estimated; the same is true for a USD price.

products.name: SunSun HW-304B Canister Filter with UV Sterilizer
products.priceNote: Walmart's US listing for the "Sunsun Hw304B 525GPH Pro Canister Filter Kit with 9-watt UV Sterilizer" shows "Current price is USD $178.99". SunSun has no dedicated US manufacturer storefront; pricing comes from US retailers/importers.
products.provenance: Ming Trading LLC's US distributor product page for the HW-304B states: "525 GPH (2000L/hr)" flow rate, "good for up to 150 gallon fish tanks", pump power "55W" stated separately from the integrated "9W" UV sterilizer bulb (55W used for wattage — the pump, not the UV lamp), a "5-stage system" with "4 media trays", and dimensions "11in L x 11in W x 17in H". Aquatic Rig's listing independently confirms a "Self-priming pump" feature (self_priming=true). Walmart's US listing confirms the $178.99 price for this exact SKU ("Pro Canister Filter Kit with 9-watt UV Sterilizer", matching the HW-304B's built-in-UV model designation, distinguishing it from the plain HW-304 without UV). No media basket volume in liters is disclosed (media is specified only by weight/count — 1lb carbon, 1lb ceramic rings, 40 bio balls), so media_capacity_l is null.

products.name: OASE BioMaster Thermo 850 Canister Filter
products.priceNote: Only a EUR price could be sourced from a fetched page (aquaristikshop.com: €349.85, a German retailer), not a verbatim US-dollar figure, so priceUsd is left null rather than converted/guessed. This is a EU-manufactured product line with limited US retail presence.
products.provenance: The German retailer aquaristikshop.com's product page for the current-generation "BioMaster² Thermo 850" (OASE's own product-family page, cited as corroboration, confirms this is the model sold under the BioMaster Thermo 850 name in English markets) states verbatim: pump flow "1500 l/h" (≈400 US GPH, the rounder figure independently used by several English-language aquarium retailers, so 400 is used for flow_rate_gph), pump power consumption "32 Watt", a separate integrated "400 W" heater (not blended into the wattage field — see methodologyNotes), maximum tank size "bis zu 850 Liter" (≈225 US gal by strict conversion, but English-market retailers consistently market this exact model as "up to 250 gallons (850L)", the figure used here), dimensions "240 x 240 x 535 mm" (converted to 9.4 x 9.4 x 21.1 in), and "filter volume: 8.0 liters". The page describes four distinct filtration stages (mechanical, biological, optional chemical, and customizable media), used for media_stages=4. A separate OASE product description for the closely related BioMaster Thermo 600 states "the self-priming function guarantees easy start-ups" — the same pump/priming mechanism used across the whole BioMaster Thermo range — so self_priming is set true for the 850 as well. No US-dollar price could be sourced.

products.name: Marineland Penguin 350 (BIO-Wheel) Power Filter
products.priceNote: No verbatim USD price could be sourced from a fetched page: Marineland's own product page does not list one, and retailer search snippets (Amazon, Walmart, eBay) never surfaced an actual dollar figure in fetched content.
products.provenance: Marineland's official Penguin Power Filters page identifies the "PF0350B Marineland Penguin Power Filter 350 GPH" (flow_rate_gph=350) and describes the whole Penguin BIO-Wheel line as "three-stage mechanical, chemical and biological aquarium filtration" (media_stages=3). The retail packaging (used as the image) prints "BIO-WHEEL PENGUIN 350 POWER FILTER", "350 gallons per hour", and "75 gallon aquarium" rated size, confirming tank_size_gal=75; this exact "up to 75 gallon" figure is also repeated consistently across independent third-party retail listings for the PF0350B. Marineland's own page does not state a wattage figure, media basket volume, or physical dimensions for this model, and no reliably-sourced third-party page supplied them either (one forum comment cited 14W, but a single unverified forum mention was not treated as sufficient sourcing), so those fields plus self_priming (never addressed on the fetched page) and priceUsd are left null.
